brief: An unmade bed seen from directly above. Its rumpled sheet is rendered as if carved shallowly into laterite-pink sandstone. Raking light from the far left throws every fold into crisp lit ridges and deep incised troughs, like a temple frieze. Build it with layered graphite under thin washes of rose-ochre and grey-green lichen watercolour. Pencil gives the carved edges a chiselled precision, and the washes add mottled stone weathering. The composition fills the frame edge to edge as a dense horizontal band of rhythmic drapery. There is no background and no horizon, only the relief continuing past the borders.

A steamed bathroom mirror with one diagonal swath wiped clear by a palm. Through that swath, a man's lathered jaw and a razor mid-stroke appear in crisp coloured-pencil hyperrealism: stubble, foam bubbles and a nick of carmine. Everywhere else, wet-into-wet watercolour fog rolls in pearl grey and warm breath-white. Soft blooms swallow the teal tile and the towel behind. Drips run down from the wipe's edge in sharp little channels. The contrast between the soft, smothering haze and the one surgical window drives the piece.

A close, slightly overhead view of a mud-caked running shoe whose lace is tied in a doubled bow. The hyperreal render, with grit in the mesh and a frayed aglet, is crossed by the clarity of a topology diagram. Each lace strand carries a crisp black fine-liner outline, and every under-crossing breaks with a tidy white gap. Flat alcohol-marker fills sit in safety orange, mud brown and scuffed grey, with a few precise pen highlights. The ground is pale graph-paper blue. The tangle is studied, numbered by eye, part sneaker and part proof.

A swimmer turning to breathe in an outdoor lido, goggles fogged, a mouth half open, water sheeting off a shoulder. The colour follows cross-processed film. Shadows go cyan-teal, highlights blow out to chartreuse yellow, skin turns a strange peach-magenta, and contrast is brutal. Gritty spray grain covers everything. Marker blocks the deep shadows hard, and pen picks out droplets and goggle-strap detail. The crop is tilted, close and slightly blurred at the edges like a snapshot. It feels summery, punchy and late-nineties.

A slab of honeycomb tilted on a plate, honey sagging off its edge. It is rendered like a Tiffany-era leaded lampshade. Thick black marker lines work as lead cames, tracing every hexagon wall and the drip outline. Each cell is filled with streaky, opalescent watercolour glazes: amber, topaz, butterscotch and milky cream, with cooler green glass where the plate shows through. The honey surface is hyperreal, with trapped bubbles, wax caps and long refractive strands. Light seems to come from within the glass. The mood is warm, ornamental and Edwardian-lavish.

A heap of dynamic climbing ropes on lichen-flecked granite, arranged into strict Celtic over-under interlace with no loose ends. Ropes in magenta, electric blue and lime pass alternately over and under in a balanced knot that fills a square frame. The medium is graphite pencil for the rock and for the rope twist shadows. Coloured pencil burnishing builds every braided sheath fibre, fray and chalk smudge. The ground is a cool grey granite texture. It should feel like a medieval manuscript knot discovered at a crag, both meditative and athletic.

Three syrups pour over a mound of shaved ice in a footed cream bowl: amber caramel, jade-green matcha and ivory condensed milk. The palette borrows sancai glaze's three colours, and the syrups behave like that glaze running down a kiln-fired body. The medium is wet-in-wet watercolour that bleeds and pools where the colours meet, leaving hard tide-lines and speckled granulation. Crisp dry-brush highlights and tiny pencil facets pick out the individual ice crystals, so they read as frozen and sharp. The view is three-quarter from slightly above, against a warm oatmeal ground. The mood is sticky, glossy and slowly running.

A cracked walnut beside an old iron nutcracker on rumpled linen, drawn the way a copperplate etching is engraved. Everything is fine pen in warm sepia-black. Form comes from swelling and tapering parallel lines, cross-hatching and stipple, with no flat tone anywhere. The brain-like kernel lobes, the woody septum and the linen weave each get their own hatching system. A faint wiped plate-tone wash of raw umber sits behind everything, with a bevelled plate-mark border. Light comes from upper left and is printmaker-dramatic. It should look like a nineteenth-century scientific engraving pushed to photographic exactness.

An opened electrical junction box seen dead-on, its bundle of insulated wires laid out like a transit diagram. The wire colours are brown, blue, green-yellow, red, white and black. They run in strict horizontals, verticals and forty-five-degree bends and terminate in brass screw terminals like station stops. The base is technical pen and flat marker on a clean off-white enamel plate. The realism sits in the copper strands, scuffed PVC sheen and a dusty screw head. It is crisp, ordered and diagrammatic, yet you can almost smell warm plastic.

Tomatoes arranged as a Munsell colour-chip chart on a neutral grey card. Each fruit sits in a precise grid cell, stepping across from hard jade green through breaker blush and orange to deep oxblood red. Down the grid, value darkens in measured steps. Each tomato is rendered in opaque, matte watercolour with hyperreal calyx hairs, stem scars and a single soft highlight. Tiny pencil notation labels each cell, and a few cells sit deliberately empty. The mood is clinical, quiet and systematic, appetising almost by accident.

Halved blood orange, split figs and pomegranate seeds on a polished nero marquina slab, rendered as pietra dura hardstone inlay. Each colour region is a flat, hard-edged watercolour fill: carnelian, jasper red, lapis, malachite, chalcedony white. Inside each fill, stone veining and mottling stay subtle. Hairline pen seams separate every piece, like cut stone fitted together. Hyperreal accuracy survives in the shapes, specular glints and seed juiciness, but the surface reads as cold, glossy and mineral. The composition is a symmetric Florentine tabletop arrangement viewed straight down, jewel-like and opulent.

A sleeping newborn's face, cheek squashed against a blanket, rendered like a false-colour radio-telescope image. The colour is mapped by intensity: deep indigo at the edges, through teal and acid-free sodium yellow, to near-white at the warm nose and lips. The whole surface is built from dense sprayed speckle, like sensor noise. In the brightest zones it resolves into hyperreal milia, eyelashes and lip peel drawn in fine pencil. Dark navy fills the margins, with faint survey gridlines and a tiny scale bar. The result feels scientific and distant, yet unbearably tender.

An elderly man's ear and jaw seen in profile against a low setting sun. The cartilage glows translucent cadmium-red and coral where light passes through it. Silver peach fuzz and stray hairs form a rim halo of single, hair-thin pencil strokes. Underneath, layered watercolour washes go from warm sienna to rose madder, and dense coloured pencil builds pores, creases and liver spots. The background melts into an out-of-focus wash of apricot and Naples yellow with no detail. The crop is tight and off-centre, with the ear filling the upper right. The feeling is tender and intimate, almost reverent about ageing skin.

A stepped pyramid of old wooden matchboxes, each box edge chip-notched in tramp-art zigzags. A single match flares at the top in daylight. Warm brown pencil and sepia pen hatching build the layered, notched ridges, so the stack looks carved and whittled, with every chevron casting a crisp shadow. Faded paper labels in brick red and mustard are rendered with peeling, foxed hyperreal detail. Scattered spent match heads lie at the base. Light rakes from the side to stress the chip-carved rhythm. It feels patient, homespun and obsessive.

A ballpark hot dog in a paper tray, loaded with a mustard zigzag, ketchup and relish. It is rendered hyperreal but printed like a vintage Sunday comics page. Marker fills use a limited newsprint set of primary red, process yellow, flat cyan and their overlaps. Each colour layer is slightly misregistered against a confident, brushy black ink contour. The paper ground is pale yellowed newsprint with subtle grain. Despite the flat colour, the sausage skin blisters, bun crumb and glistening relish are almost absurdly precise. It should feel cheerful, loud and nostalgic, framed in a single comic panel border.

Strawberries frozen in an ice-cube tray, seen from above, with feathery frost ferns branching across the plastic and over the fruit. The strawberries are hyperreal watercolour in alizarin, carmine and seed-yellow, muted under the ice. The frost is countless fine white and pale cerulean pen strokes following flowing branched paths, fractal, feathered and crystalline. The cool blue-grey ground has misty bloom where the ice is thicker. The fruit should feel trapped and preserved beneath a crackling, intricate skin of cold.

A child's bare feet resting on a red-and-white gingham picnic blanket beside a bitten peach, all under a summer tree canopy. The base is watercolour, keeping the gingham's woven texture. Over it, soft sprayed pools of warm light and cool viridian shade drift across the scene in coin-shaped blotches. Within each light spot the detail sharpens to hyperreal: toe creases, grass stains, peach fuzz and wet flesh. In shade the forms soften. A few grass blades and an ant are rendered in fine pen. The mood is lazy, warm and flickering, like a held afternoon breath.

Two cupped palms seen from above, holding a pool of water. The skin's creases, knuckles and fingerprints are mapped as dense bathymetric contour lines in fine sepia pen, with isolines tightening over ridges and widening across the flat palm. Graded watercolour depth-tints pool in stepped bands, from pale sea-glass to cerulean to Prussian blue at the deepest centre of the water. A few contours carry tiny unreadable sounding marks. It reads as a nautical chart at first glance and only slowly resolves into living, wet hands.

An extreme close view of a worn toothbrush head, in the manner of a scanning electron micrograph. The splayed nylon bristles become towering columns with frayed, split tips, and a smear of toothpaste becomes a cratered paste-landscape. The image is entirely monochrome, in charcoal mass and silver graphite, with the characteristic SEM edge-glow: rims bright, recesses inky black. Depth recedes into soft grey fog. A tiny scale bar sits in a corner strip in thin pen, with no numbers. The surface is velvety and dusty, smudged by finger blending.

A worker's calloused hand gripping a cordless power drill, thrust along a steep diagonal across the sheet. Hand and drill are rendered in photographic graphite with grime in the knuckle creases and scuffed plastic, and they look cut out like photomontage. Behind them, flat marker-filled wedges of vermilion and solid black slice the space, with a cream circle and a heavy black bar of blocky faux-lettering. Small metal shavings spiral from the drill bit. The tension comes from the push between machine-precise graphic planes and tactile, sweaty realism.
